To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expiration-based scheme can be effectively managed by a distribution tree, and a new algorithm is proposed to efficiently construct the tree for a given replica configuration.

the optimal distribution tree for the expiration-based consistency management is NP-complete; the shortest-paths algorithm is optimal for the case of a complete binary tree; the minimum spanning tree is suboptimal in general; the proposed heuristic algorithms are able to achieve good performance.
the optimal solution to the minimal cost distribution tree is the minimum spanning tree, and the optimal solution can be computed by the heuristic algorithms with the cost within 1.5% of the optimal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the design of a cost-efficient distribution tree for consistency management of replicated contents.
the construction of an efficient distribution tree for consistency management in a multi-replica environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heuristic algorithms are more efficient than the classical algorithms in terms of communication cost.
the proposed algorithms outperform the shortest-paths and minimum spanning tree algorithms in terms of communication cost.
the heuristic algorithms are able to construct trees with a total cost comparable to the minimum spanning tree and with a significantly lower cost than the shortest-paths algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the heuristic algorithms are more efficient than the graph-theoretic ones, and the heuristic algorithms are also more efficient than the optimal solution for the cases where the optimal solution is known.
the shortest-path tree algorithm performs the best among all the algorithms tested.
the heuristic algorithms are very efficient in practice and the shortest-path tree is a good approximation to the optimal distribution tree.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the expiration-based consistency management, a shortest-paths tree is not necessarily a good solution.
the optimal distribution tree is not always the shortest-paths or the minimum spanning tree.
, in the context of expiration-based consistency management, a distribution tree constructed based on a shortest-paths metric is not necessarily optimal.
